study_identification_part.si_4_title: Neurofind: using deep learning to make individualised inferences in brain-based disorders

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study uses an adversarial autoencoder (AAE) for the Outlier Detection normative model. The AAE learns a latent representation of disease-free brain morphology by forcing the latent code distribution to match a Gaussian prior. The architecture comprises an input layer with 101 neurons, an encoder with one hidden layer (25 neurons), a latent code with 5 neurons, a decoder with one hidden layer (25 neurons), and a discriminator. A separate linear support vector regression (SVR) model was used for brain age prediction, but this serves as a secondary metric rather than the primary normative model.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Our outlier detection model uses an adversarial autoencoder (AAE) to learn a representation of disease-free brain morphology. Briefly, AAE combines a standard autoencoder with adversarial learning to improve the learned latent representation by forcing it to have a distribution similar to a desired prior distribution. In our approach, we used a Gaussian distribution.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study models relative brain region volumes (ROIrel) from 101 brain regions: 68 cortical regions (34 per hemisphere) from the Desikan-Killiany atlas and 33 subcortical/other structures from the ASEG atlas in FreeSurfer. The ROIrel values were calculated by dividing original brain region volumes by total intracranial volume (TIV). Cortical regions include volumes from gyri and cortical structures, while subcortical regions include structures such as hippocampus, amygdala, caudate, putamen, pallidum, thalamus, cerebellum, ventricles, and corpus callosum.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The cortical surface was parcellated using the Desikan-Killiany cortical atlas and segmented into 68 cortical regions (34 per hemisphere). An additional 33 neuroanatomical structures were extracted using the ASEG atlas in FreeSurfer totalling 101 brain regions (ROIs)... We estimated the relative brain region volumes (ROIrel) for each subject by dividing the original brain region volumes by the total intracranial volume

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The AAE normative model was conditioned on age and sex as explanatory variables. These demographic variables were incorporated so that the model learns a latent representation while accounting for age and sex effects. For the Neuroharmony scanner harmonization, age and sex were also used as covariates for the Outlier Detection model, while only sex was used for the Brain Age model.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: To further account for the effect of demographics variables, age and sex were added to the model such that the AAE was conditioned to learn a latent representation whilst taking into account this information.
